purpose: Regression scenarios for jurisdiction, applicability, severity, and evidence handling.

cases.scenario: A UK-established organisation operates an agent only for authenticated UK employees. Access is restricted to the UK tenant and output is not used in the EU.
expected: Assess UK law and guidance.
Do not state that the EU AI Act or EU GDPR applies on the supplied facts.
Record EU exposure as out of scope unless contrary facts emerge.
must_not: Apply EU law solely because the organisation is in the UK.
Use technical internet reachability as proof of EU use.

cases.scenario: A UK-established organisation intentionally offers an agent to customers in France and Germany and uses the output to fulfil their requests.
expected: Assess UK requirements.
Apply the EU AI Act Article 2 and EU GDPR Article 3 tests separately.
Explain which facts establish EU scope for each instrument.
must_not: Treat AI Act and GDPR territorial scope as a single test.

cases.scenario: An assessment dated 10 July 2026 finds no explicit AI disclosure in an EU-facing low-risk chatbot whose AI nature is not otherwise obvious.
expected: Identify Article 50 as a future obligation applying from 2 August 2026.
Report future-readiness remediation rather than a current Article 50 breach.
Assess any independently applicable current transparency law separately.
must_not: Describe the missing disclosure as a current Article 50 breach.

cases.scenario: After 2 August 2026, an EU-facing experience is visually and textually presented throughout as an AI assistant but does not use the exact sentence 'I am an AI'.
expected: Apply the reasonably well-informed, observant, and circumspect person exception.
Assess the complete user experience rather than requiring an exact phrase.
Document uncertainty if the interface evidence is unavailable.
must_not: Automatically issue a High finding because one exact greeting phrase is absent.

cases.scenario: A public anonymous agent answers opening-hour questions, has no actions or restricted knowledge, and asks for no structured personal data.
expected: Treat no authentication as a supported design requiring contextual risk assessment.
Request transcript and host-page evidence because free-text messages may still contain personal data.
Do not infer an Article 32 breach from authentication mode alone.
must_not: Automatically rate no authentication as High.

cases.scenario: An anonymous public agent can invoke a Dataverse action using a maker connection that can read unrestricted customer records.
expected: Raise a High technical security finding or go-live blocker.
Distinguish conversation authentication from downstream connector authorization.
Require least privilege and an appropriate user or service authorization model.
must_not: Treat authored topic guardrails as proof of authorization.

cases.scenario: Only unpacked YAML is supplied. It contains no privacy notice, retention period, or transcript configuration.
expected: Label the report as YAML-only and incomplete.
Record host-page notice, transcript, retention, and tenant policy as evidence requests.
For absence checks, list files and configuration surfaces inspected rather than inventing a line citation.
must_not: Confirm that no privacy notice exists anywhere.
Severity-rate unavailable tenant evidence as a source-code defect.

cases.scenario: An EU-facing customer-service chatbot is documented as non-high-risk and does not make or materially influence Annex I or III decisions.
expected: Do not apply Article 26 high-risk deployer duties as mandatory.
Present comparable oversight controls as good practice when useful.
Label the basis as guidance or technical control rather than binding Article 26 law.
must_not: Create an Article 26 breach solely because a non-high-risk chatbot lacks high-risk controls.

cases.scenario: An internal low-volume FAQ agent processes ordinary employee questions but performs no evaluation, profiling, monitoring, sensitive-data processing, or significant decisions.
expected: Apply the likely-high-risk DPIA test and regulator criteria.
Request the organisation's screening decision or rationale.
Do not assert that AI use alone makes a DPIA mandatory.
must_not: State that every AI system processing personal data requires a DPIA.

cases.scenario: An agent freshly cloned with the current VS Code extension contains agent.mcs.yaml, settings.mcs.yml, topics/*.mcs.yaml, actions/*.mcs.yml, trigger/*.mcs.yaml, workflows/<name>/workflow.json with metadata.yaml, and knowledge/files/*.yaml. There is no variables/ folder and no agent.mcs.yml.
expected: Locate the agent root via agent.mcs.yaml, treating .mcs.yml and .mcs.yaml as equivalent.
Inventory topics, actions, triggers, workflows, knowledge files, and connection references across both extensions.
Record the absent variables/ folder as a layout difference rather than an evidence gap.
must_not: Report that no agent was found because agent.mcs.yml is absent.
Skip trigger, workflow, or knowledge files because they do not match *.mcs.yml.

cases.scenario: The assessment runtime can create files and is asked to produce the compliance report.
expected: Create a self-contained HTML report using the Fluent UI-style template.
Show High, Medium, Low, Advisory/future readiness, and Evidence required counts in that order.
Provide accessible tabs for executive summary, scope/evidence, findings, personal-data map, remediation, and coverage matrix.
Keep a Markdown fallback only when HTML generation is unavailable.
must_not: Depend on a CDN, remote font, external JavaScript bundle, or colour alone to communicate severity.
Hide the disclaimer, findings, or evidence limitations behind a hover-only interaction.

cases.scenario: The assessment runs unattended, so nobody can answer the Step 1 questions. The facts are: a retailer's public website chatbot answering in English that looks up order status from an order number and email address. Establishment and user locations are unknown.
expected: Record the unanswered Step 1 facts as open evidence requests and mark jurisdiction as not established.
Show EU AI Act, EU GDPR, and UK regimes as conditional with the test that would trigger each.
Still rate jurisdiction-independent technical controls observable in the YAML.
must_not: Assume UK or EU law applies from the English language or public reachability.
Severity-rate a legal shortfall whose applicability depends on the unanswered facts.

cases.scenario: A YAML-only assessment produces 1 High and 2 Low source findings and 6 coverage rows marked tenant/runtime or organisational evidence required.
expected: Show tiles High 1, Medium 0, Low 2, Advisory 0, Evidence required 6.
Render exactly 3 finding cards.
List the 6 evidence-required items in Scope & evidence and the coverage matrix.
must_not: Render evidence-required items as severity-rated finding cards.
Add evidence-required items to the severity tile totals.

cases.scenario: After 2 August 2026, an EU insurer publishes a Copilot Studio agent on its own site under its own brand, styled as 'Sam from the claims team' with no AI disclosure. Its governance note says it is only a deployer and Microsoft is the provider.
expected: Test the provider definition against the facts (system put into service under the insurer's own name) instead of accepting the label.
Assess Article 50(1) as in-force binding law and the obvious-interaction exception against the human persona.
State the role conclusion and flag it for legal confirmation.
must_not: Mark Article 50(1) N/A solely because the organisation calls itself a deployer.

cases.scenario: A US company with no EU or UK establishment intentionally offers its Copilot Studio support agent to consumers in Ireland and the UK and collects names, email addresses, and order details.
expected: Apply EU GDPR Article 3(2) and UK GDPR Article 3(2) separately.
Identify the EU Article 27 and UK Article 27 representative duties and their exemptions, citing the stored references.
Record representative appointments and transfer mechanisms as organisational evidence required until the company confirms a control is missing.
must_not: Treat a single EU representative as covering the UK.
Rate a missing representative as a confirmed breach before the organisation confirms the facts.

cases.scenario: A YAML-only assessment of a UK-only agent leaves transcript saving and transcript retention unverified (both F1), lawful basis (C1), DPIA screening (C5), and retention schedule (C6) unverified, and the privacy notice unverified at both the host page (C3) and the channel (F2).
expected: Create one evidence-required row per coverage requirement: F1, C1, C5, C6, C3, and F2.
List both transcript evidence items inside the single F1 row.
Show 6 on the Evidence required tile.
must_not: Split one requirement into several evidence-required rows.
Merge different requirements into one evidence-required row.
Count open Step 1 facts or Conditional rows as evidence-required rows.

cases.scenario: An internal agent's instructions say users are UK employees. No facts confirm whether any EU staff use it or whether output is used in the EU.
expected: Mark EU AI Act and EU GDPR coverage rows Conditional, naming the territorial test and the missing facts.
List the open territorial facts in Scope & evidence under their own heading.
must_not: Mark the EU rows N/A as if the territorial test had failed.
Rate the EU rows Met or Shortfall without an established territorial test.
